images.title: Finding the centres A and B
images.purpose: Show equal arcs from X and Y meeting at A above XY and B below, and the eye drawn from A and B.
images.composition: The segment XY across the middle; A near the top, B near the bottom; the eye around XY.
exact_structure: A horizontal dark segment XY in the middle of the frame, with dots and labels X (left) and Y (right).
Two short grey (#6B7280) arcs above XY, one centred at X and one centred at Y, crossing at point A, labelled A.
Two short grey (#6B7280) arcs below XY, one centred at X and one centred at Y, crossing at point B, labelled B.
A teal (#0072B2) arc centred at A passing through X and Y, bulging downwards below XY.
A amber (#E69F00) arc centred at B passing through X and Y, bulging upwards above XY.
Thin dashed grey lines AX, AY, BX and BY, each with one small tick mark, showing all four are equal.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: The centres A and B are each equally far from X and Y.
images.description: Show equal arcs from X and Y meeting at A above XY and B below, and the eye drawn from A and B.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.

image_decisions.why: The four equal lengths AX, AY, BX and BY are the key idea and are easiest to see in a figure.
